conditions.L: Identical fixed statement and P62 shared files plus frozen NumStability library.
conditions.N: Identical fixed statement and P62 shared files; no NumStability artifact.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p62_t1_method1_inverse_right_residual (fp : P62FPModel) (n : ℕ) ... : |I−L·X| ≤ γ_n |L|·|X| entrywise
formal_statement.plain_language: Method 1’s columnwise computed lower-triangular inverse has componentwise right residual |I−LX| bounded entrywise by γ_n |L||X|.

informal_proof: Apply the paper’s perturbed forward-substitution relation separately to each inverse column and rewrite the right residual as the action of that column’s coefficient perturbation.
informal_statement: Method 1’s columnwise computed lower-triangular inverse has componentwise right residual |I−LX| bounded entrywise by γ_n |L||X|.
paper_version: published journal version; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis 12(1), 1992, printed pages 1-19

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: Both exact private N/L proofs compile; N has no NumStability import; L directly uses one substantial frozen result.

tier_rationale: The L proof directly calls the substantial frozen forwardSub_backward_error theorem for one arbitrary-size triangular solve and applies it to each inverse column. N reconstructs the full forward-substitution perturbation argument; the residual rewrite is elementary. N is 757 lines versus L 100; Mathlib supplies no triangular-solve rounding analysis.
